# Introduction

This document details the process of cleaning, preparing, and analyzing humoral data related to HBV vaccination. The analysis involves several steps, including data import, merging of different batches, handling of duplicates, and integration of metadata. The primary goal is to explore the antibody responses over time, particularly in different age groups and vaccine types.

```{r block1-importdata}
# Block 1: Data Import and Library Loading

# This section loads all the necessary R packages for data manipulation, visualization, and statistical analysis.
library(reshape)      # Data reshaping
library(reshape2)     # More data reshaping
library(ggplot2)      # Plotting

        axis.text.y = element_text(color = "black"),
        text = element_text(family = "Arial"),
        plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5),

# Calculate arithmetic mean and confidence intervals.
df.alum.mean <- df.alum %>% #arith mean
  filter(group == "Alum") %>%
  filter(!timepoint == "v3w3") %>%
  group_by(timepoint, age_group) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), mean=mean(elisa),
            median = median(elisa),
            sd = sd(elisa)) %>%
  mutate(sem = sd / sqrt(n - 1),
         CI_lower = mean + qt((1-0.95)/2, n - 1) * sem,
         CI_upper = mean - qt((1-0.95)/2, n - 1) * sem)

# Plot the arithmetic mean with confidence intervals.

# --- Geometric Mean and Quartiles ---
# Functions are defined to calculate geometric mean and quartiles for visualization.
geo_mean <- function(x) {
  x <- x[x > 0]          
  if (length(x) == 0) {  
    return(NA_real_)
  }
  exp(mean(log(x)))
}

    Q3 = exp(quantile(log(elisa), 0.75, na.rm = TRUE)),
    .groups = "drop"

# Define a function to calculate geometric mean and quartiles.
geo_summary <- function(x) {
  x <- x[x > 0]  
  if (length(x) == 0) return(data.frame(y = NA, ymin = NA, ymax = NA))
  logx <- log(x)
  data.frame(
    y    = exp(mean(logx)),                         # geometric mean
    ymin = exp(quantile(logx, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE)), # Q1
    ymax = exp(quantile(logx, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE))  # Q3
  )
}

  adjust_pvalue(method = "BH") %>%

  add_xy_position(x = "timepoint", dodge = 0.8)

  mutate(y.position = c(2.8, 3, 3, 3, 2.7)[seq_len(n())])

# Define a function to calculate geometric mean and 95% confidence intervals.
geo_mean_CI <- function(x) {
  x <- x[x > 0]  # drop non-positive values
  if (length(x) == 0) return(data.frame(y = NA, ymin = NA, ymax = NA))
  logx <- log(x)
  n <- length(logx)
  mean_log <- mean(logx)
  se_log <- sd(logx) / sqrt(n)
  # 95% CI on log scale
  CI_lower <- mean_log - 1.96 * se_log
  CI_upper <- mean_log + 1.96 * se_log
  data.frame(
    y = exp(mean_log),       # geometric mean
    ymin = exp(CI_lower),    # lower CI
    ymax = exp(CI_upper)     # upper CI
  )
}

# --- Linear Mixed-Effects Model ---
# A linear mixed-effects model (LME) is used to analyze the interaction between timepoint and age group.
# The following commented out code shows a basic LME model.
# df.alum %>%
#   #mutate(log_elisa = log(elisa)) %>%
#   lmer(log(elisa) ~ timepoint * age_group + (1 | subject), data = .) %>%
#   anova()

# Basic LME model
fit <- lmer(log(elisa) ~ timepoint * age_group + (1|subject), data = df.alum)
aov_tab <- anova(fit)
pval <- signif(aov_tab["timepoint:age_group", "Pr(>F)"], 3)
pval
summary(fit)
# The following commented out code shows how to get p-values using Kenward-Roger's approximation.
#anova(fit, ddf = "Kenward-Roger")

# LME model adjusting for baseline
temp <- df.alum %>%
  filter(!subject == "0082") %>% #no v1w0
  group_by(subject) %>%
  mutate(
    baseline_log_elisa = log(elisa[timepoint == "v1w0"])
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

temp$sex <- factor(temp$sex)

fit <- lmer(
  log(elisa) ~ baseline_log_elisa + 
    #sex + bmi + age + 
    timepoint * age_group + (1 | subject),
  data = temp
)
aov_tab <- anova(fit)
pval <- signif(aov_tab["timepoint:age_group", "Pr(>F)"], 3)

  scale_y_log10(labels = scales::label_number()) +
  ct2 +
  scale_x_discrete(expand = c(0,0)) +
  annotate("text", x = 5, y = 800, 
           label = paste0("Interaction p = ", pval),
```
